page.layout: One column of running text, with marginal notes in the right margin (side notes at lines 1, the "Vir justus" line and the "Qui enim" line). Printed page number 123 at top right; running head at top left. Catchword "ventum" below the last line.

main_text.p: Cafus 29Cafus ergo primus est, ubi metus est levis, & qui non facile cadit in constantem virum: ut siquis metu iniquæ censuræ, vel irrisionis, vel iræ & offensionis alicujus viri potentis, juramento se promitteret facturum aliquid quod sibi esset inconveniens, quodque ni metus ille esset, nec facere vellet nec promittere. Pro refponsione illud imprimis repeten-lum est, quod in tota hac materiâ ju-amentariâ est sanctissimè observandum, [?]quid proponatur juandum[?], quod est [?]contra legem Dei, [?]contra officium hominis Christiani, contra bonos mores, contra leges Reip. contra antecedentem obligationem, aut alio quocunque efpectu illicitum: non debere ullo aut [?]commodi intuitu, aut periculi metu, e-ufmodi juramentum aut præstari, aut præstitum adimpleri. Hoc [?]lico, viro forti (id est pio; pius enim esse nequit qui non est fortis) simpliciter contemnendum esse inanem & levem metum, & omne ejusmodi juramentum constanter & intrepidè recusandum. Nimirum est {i}Pro.23.1.Vir justus fortis ut leo; qua fortitudine qui destitutus est, vix ieri potest ut faciat insigne aliquid viro [?]bono dignum. {k}Eccl.11. 4.Qui enim observat

page.notes: The left edge of the scan is cropped, so the first letters of several lines are partly lost; these are marked [?] or reconstructed (quid, contra, commodi, lico, bono, ieri). "juandum" and "repeten-lum" are as far as the visible letters allow; "lum" may be a cropped "dum". The line "Hoc [?]lico" is unclear. The paragraph runs on across all lines because no line ends short or is indented. The bullet mark before "ventum" is omitted. The note "Eccl.11. 4." is split across the page: "Eccl.11." beside the text and "4." at the foot of the margin.
